title: Extending the Oracle Approximating Shrinkage to General Distributions
abstract: arXiv:2610.22144v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The Oracle Approximating Shrinkage (OAS) estimator provides a closed-form, data-driven shrinkage intensity for regularizing sample covariance matrices toward a scaled identity target, but its derivation assumes Gaussian data. In practice, financial returns, neural signals, and many other high-dimensional datasets exhibit heavy tails and non-zero kurtosis, violating this assumption. We extend OAS to any distribution with finite fourth moments by incorporating a correction term $\alpha$ built from the fourth-order joint cumulants of the data. The correction vanishes under Gaussianity, recovering the OAS formula as a special case; it admits a consistent $O(np)$ sample estimator and satisfies $\rho \in [0, 1]$ exactly for both the population cumulant and its sample analogue. Simulations and an equity-returns study confirm that the correction closes the gap between OAS and the Ledoit-Wolf estimator under non-Gaussian data, with OAS-Extended

translated_title: 将Oracle近似收缩估计（OAS）扩展至一般分布
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.22144v1 公告类型：cross 摘要：Oracle近似收缩（OAS）估计器为将样本协方差矩阵向缩放单位阵目标进行正则化提供了一种闭式、数据驱动的收缩强度，但其推导假设数据服从高斯分布。在实际应用中，金融收益率、神经信号以及许多其他高维数据集往往呈现重尾和非零峰度特征，违背了这一假设。我们通过引入一个由数据四阶联合累积量构建的修正项 α，将OAS扩展到任何具有有限四阶矩的分布。该修正在高斯情形下会消失，从而将原OAS公式作为特例恢复；它拥有一个一致的 O(np) 复杂度样本估计量，并且无论是总体累积量还是其样本对应量，均严格满足收缩强度 ρ ∈ [0, 1]。仿真实验和股票收益率实证研究表明，该修正项在非高斯数据下缩小了OAS与Ledoit-Wolf估计器之间的性能差距，OAS扩展版本（OAS-Extended）……
tldr: 该论文通过一个由四阶联合累积量构建、在高斯情形下自动消失的修正项，将原本仅适用于高斯数据的OAS协方差收缩估计器扩展到任意具有有限四阶矩的重尾分布，保证收缩强度严格落在[0,1]区间，并在非高斯数据下达到与Ledoit-Wolf估计器相当的性能。
en_tdlr: This paper extends the Gaussian-assumption OAS covariance shrinkage estimator to any distribution with finite fourth moments by introducing a correction term built from fourth-order joint cumulants, which vanishes under Gaussianity, keeps the shrinkage intensity strictly in [0,1], and closes the performance gap with the Ledoit-Wolf estimator on heavy-tailed, non-Gaussian data.
